evidence.claim: Amnesty says the government continued stigmatizing feminists and human rights defenders, security forces used violence against women protesters, journalist killings remained at record levels, more than 109,000 people were missing at year-end, militarization of domestic security was extended through 2028, and the National Guard used excessive force in several operations.
evidence.title: Mexiko 2022 | Amnesty International Report 2022/23
evidence.excerpt: Amnesty says the government continued stigmatizing feminists and human rights defenders, security forces used violence against women protesters, journalist killings remained at record levels, more than 109,000 people were missing at year-end, militarization of domestic security was extended through 2028, and the National Guard used excessive force in several operations.
evidence.source_locator: Background / freedom of expression / excessive force / disappearances sections
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Annual rights report with clear 2022 coverage and concrete event-level allegations.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Mostly state and security-force conduct under AMLO; some incidents are state-level or operational rather than direct presidential orders.
contrary_evidence: The report also notes some remedies and judicial steps in individual cases, including Ayotzinapa.
It is a rights-monitoring synthesis, not a court finding for every incident.

evidence.claim: ARTICLE 19 reports 696 attacks on the press in 2022, one every 13 hours; 42.53% were committed directly by state actors; the executive branch made stigmatising comments at least 176 times; and 10 media companies received 54.8% of government advertising spend.
evidence.title: Mexico: Voices Against Indifference
evidence.excerpt: ARTICLE 19 reports 696 attacks on the press in 2022, one every 13 hours; 42.53% were committed directly by state actors; the executive branch made stigmatising comments at least 176 times; and 10 media companies received 54.8% of government advertising spend.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Detailed annual press-freedom dataset from a specialized monitor, with clear 2022 statistics.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strongly relevant to AMLO-era public discourse and federal advertising control, though not every attack is directly ordered by him.
contrary_evidence: The report also notes conditions that predate AMLO, so it should not be over-read as personal command over every abuse.
Advertising concentration is a structural influence mechanism, not a complete explanation of violence.

evidence.claim: ARTICLE 19 says four journalists were killed in January 2022 and that Mexico had already recorded 28 journalist murders during López Obrador’s presidency, calling for urgent independent investigations.
evidence.title: Mexico: State must take immediate action after murder of four journalists
evidence.excerpt: ARTICLE 19 says four journalists were killed in January 2022 and that Mexico had already recorded 28 journalist murders during López Obrador’s presidency, calling for urgent independent investigations.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous rights-monitoring report with exact 2022 incident count.
evidence.ruler_attribution: The killings themselves are not all federally attributed, but the failure to stop and investigate them is relevant to AMLO-era domestic protection.
contrary_evidence: The report emphasizes investigation failures more than direct federal ordering of the killings.
It is strongest on impunity and protection failure, not on motive attribution for each murder.

evidence.claim: CPJ says at least 13 journalists had been killed in Mexico by late August 2022, the highest number it had documented in a single year, and described a climate of impunity with authorities often slow and inadequate.
evidence.title: In 2022, journalist killings continue unabated in Mexico amid a climate of impunity
evidence.excerpt: CPJ says at least 13 journalists had been killed in Mexico by late August 2022, the highest number it had documented in a single year, and described a climate of impunity with authorities often slow and inadequate.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Specialized monitor; the page is a briefing rather than a formal audit, but the numbers are specific and contemporaneous.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Applies to the AMLO-era domestic protection environment; the article does not attribute each death to the federal executive.
contrary_evidence: CPJ notes some cases may be cartel-related or hard to motive-match.
It does not separate federal from state or criminal responsibility in every case.

evidence.claim: AMLO said there was no repression, that nobody was prevented from demonstrating, and that the government had an obligation to guarantee liberties and the right to dissent; he also said women and other groups could protest.
evidence.title: Versión estenográfica de la conferencia de prensa matutina del presidente Andrés Manuel López Obrador
evidence.excerpt: AMLO said there was no repression, that nobody was prevented from demonstrating, and that the government had an obligation to guarantee liberties and the right to dissent; he also said women and other groups could protest.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary presidential transcript with direct quotes from AMLO on protest rights.
contrary_evidence: This is rhetoric and self-description, not proof that subordinate police or military behaved accordingly everywhere.
The same transcript also contains language about provocations and infiltration.

evidence.claim: After a CNDH recommendation concerning the death of Jessica Estrella Solís in a Guardia Nacional-related incident, AMLO said the cabinet had agreed to comply with the recommendation's five points.
evidence.title: Versión estenográfica de la conferencia de prensa matutina del presidente Andrés Manuel López Obrador
evidence.excerpt: After a CNDH recommendation concerning the death of Jessica Estrella Solís in a Guardia Nacional-related incident, AMLO said the cabinet had agreed to comply with the recommendation's five points.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary transcript with a specific remedy commitment tied to a rights-body recommendation.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct AMLO attribution on federal compliance with a rights-body recommendation.
contrary_evidence: The underlying incident shows lethal force by the National Guard, so the positive remedy does not erase the abuse.
The source is a self-report of compliance, not external proof of completion.

evidence.claim: The decree published in the Diario Oficial formalized reforms placing the National Guard's operational and administrative control under Sedena and changing related military and security laws.
evidence.title: DECRETO por el que se reforman, adicionan y derogan diversas disposiciones... en Materia de Guardia Nacional y Seguridad Pública
evidence.publisher: Orden Jurídico Nacional / Diario Oficial de la Federación
evidence.excerpt: The decree published in the Diario Oficial formalized reforms placing the National Guard's operational and administrative control under Sedena and changing related military and security laws.
evidence.source_locator: DOF publication notice and reform articles
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official legal text and publication record for the 2022 reform.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This reflects a presidentially driven federal policy choice under AMLO.
contrary_evidence: Supporters framed the move as administrative discipline and public safety management.
The decree does not itself prove any specific abuse, but it increases the risk of abuse and impunity.

evidence.claim: The Segob protection mechanism said it had grown from 758 people at the start of the administration to 1,508 beneficiaries by January 2022, including 495 journalists and 1,023 human rights defenders.
evidence.title: Protección a personas periodistas y defensoras de derechos humanos es obligación de Estado: Segob
evidence.excerpt: The Segob protection mechanism said it had grown from 758 people at the start of the administration to 1,508 beneficiaries by January 2022, including 495 journalists and 1,023 human rights defenders.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary government statement with concrete beneficiary counts and date.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Institutional federal protection capacity under AMLO; the data do not prove the mechanism was sufficient everywhere.
contrary_evidence: The same mechanism was still described by independent monitors as under-resourced and unable to meet all protection needs.
Growing beneficiary counts do not automatically mean successful protection.

evidence.claim: Reuters reported that at least three human rights investigators in Mexico were infected with Pegasus during López Obrador’s term despite government promises to stop using the spyware.
evidence.title: Pegasus spyware attacks in Mexico continued under Lopez Obrador -report
evidence.excerpt: Reuters reported that at least three human rights investigators in Mexico were infected with Pegasus during López Obrador’s term despite government promises to stop using the spyware.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters is a strong wire source; the specific claim is directly dated and attributable.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This is relevant to federal conduct under AMLO even if the operator of each infection is not named in the lead.
contrary_evidence: The article is based on a report, not a full forensic adjudication in the story itself.
It does not prove AMLO personally ordered every infection.

evidence.claim: The Committee said Mexico should strengthen institutions, searches and investigations, remove obstacles to taking disappearance cases to court, address the forensic crisis, facilitate truth/justice/reparation, and protect victims and searchers.
evidence.title: Report of the Committee on Enforced Disappearances on its visit to Mexico under article 33 of the Convention
evidence.publisher: United Nations Committee on Enforced Disappearances
evidence.excerpt: The Committee said Mexico should strengthen institutions, searches and investigations, remove obstacles to taking disappearance cases to court, address the forensic crisis, facilitate truth/justice/reparation, and protect victims and searchers.
evidence.source_locator: Observations and recommendations, section I and related subsections
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Authoritative UN monitoring report with direct policy recommendations after a country visit.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Applies to the AMLO administration’s handling of disappearances and investigations, though many failures sit with prosecutors, forensic institutions, and subnational authorities.
contrary_evidence: The report does not say the federal government made no progress at all.
It is a recommendations document, not a court judgment.

unresolved_gaps: Federal command attribution is still thin for several state-level protest, journalist, and policing incidents.
Independent evidence that AMLO strengthened courts, the INE, INAI, or other checks is still weak compared with the evidence of media hostility and electoral-pressure attempts.
Direct personal-nexus evidence on self-enrichment, hidden ownership, or preferential benefit remains thin, and several items are still allegations or self-reports.
Independent audit-level evidence on on-time, on-budget delivery and the causal split between AMLO policy and external tailwinds is still incomplete.
